summary: A wooden 1876 tower with its keeper's house attached, moved inland in 2009, beside two small range lights added in 1902 at Wood Islands, Prince Edward Island.

The design of the Wood Islands Lighthouse is similar to one at Cape Egmont in western PEI.
Range lights were established and put in operation on September 6,1902 to lead into Wood island harbour.
The front range tower stands on the breakwater on the south side of the east entrance to the harbour, 50 feet from its outer end.

The height of the tower from its base to the top of the ventilator on the lantern is 19 feet. The light is fixed red, elevated 18 feet above high water mark, and is visible 6 miles from all points of approach by water.
The back range tower stands on the gravel beach, 700 feet N. 85° W. from the front tower.

The height of the tower is 33 feet from its base to the top of the ventilator on the lantern. The light is fixed red catoptric, elevated 33 feet above high water mark, and is visible 7 miles in the line of range.
These buildings were erected by the agent by day labour, under the supervision of Mr. M. Walsh
James McMillan, the first keeper, was a brother of Donald McMillan who completed the construction of the lighthouse.
Keeper McMillan and his wife Lily had four sons, known as the lighthouse boys, one of whom, William, replaced his father as keeper in 1887.

The last resident keeper was Leon Patton. Wood Islands was one of the last three lighthouses to have resident keepers on PEI.
Wood Islands Lighthouse was a remote location.
many keepers preferred to travel to and from the station by rowboat.
Some children who lived at the lighthouse found it lonely, while others reveled in the adventures that could be found nearby.
James Young, the first keeper of the range lights, served from 1902 until the end of 1935, when he resigned. Harold E. Young then served from 1936 to 1943, when he too resigned.
William Robert Brown had the shortest tenure as keeper of the range lights, serving from April 1943 until his death in November 1944.

Alexander J. Young was placed in charge of the lights at the beginning of 1945, but after just three days of service, his appointment was cancelled by orders from Ottawa, and Hazel MacFarlane was reinstated.
Hazel was still serving as keeper of the range lights when they were electrified in 1963.
Wood Islands Range Lights were moved to the pier west of Wood Islands Lighthouse around 1941
A fog horn was established at Wood Islands in 1941 to aid the ferry service.
A substantial shed was attached to the front range tower in 1946 to house fog alarm equipment to operate a trumpet that protruded from the seaward side of the tower.
The lighthouse became electrified in 1958. By 1990, it had become fully automated.
In the early 1980s, the Coast Guard built a detached dwelling near the Wood Islands Lighthouse for the keeper
The detached bungalow was removed from the site in 1991.
In 1998, the Wood Islands and Area Development Cooperation opened the lighthouse to the public.
The range lights were decommissioned in 2007 and moved next to Wood Islands Lighthouse in 2013.
it stood almost 150 metres from the shore
At first light on March 10, 2009, the Wood Islands Lighthouse was uprooted and moved 70 metres (230 feet) inland.
The lighthouse was jacked up then placed on steel beams and wheels to facilitate the move, which was done during the winter when the frozen ground would provide the needed support.
Wood Islands and Area Development Corporation became the owner and operator of the Wood Islands Lighthouse Museum in December of 2009.
recognized as a heritage place under the Prince Edward Island Heritage Places Protection Act on October 3, 2012

Visitors can explore the many exhibits on display in the former keeper's residence and climb to the top of the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Coast Guard List of Lights carries Wood Islands (main lighthouse, Iso W 10s, 21.9 m) as a private aid, year round; Lighthouse Friends says the 1902 range lights were decommissioned in 2007. They concern different structures.

notes_for_editor: Mostly two Lighthouse Friends pages (copyrighted, paraphrased) and the provincial heritage text; only the 1902 report is primary. Name spellings vary (MacMillan/McMillan, MacKay/McKay). Lighthouse Friends gives 'many keepers' rowing, school and dismissal details, unverified against the 1899 House of Commons debates. Lens status and whether the main light is still lit were not confirmed (CCG list shows it as private aid). Keeper years for 1950s-70s came only from LF's list; Canadian register text cites Department of Marine tables not read. The 1904 Marine report salary table lists James Young under Wood Island Harbour but columns were not matched. Station record merges the lighthouse with the range pair; consider splitting. Fiscal 1902 report page: scan 96, printed 83 (fuzzy).
